newsitem.title: DUBAI: SOCCER-IRAQ BEAT THAILAND 4-1 TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRAQ BEAT THAILAND 4-1 TO REACH QUARTER-FINALS.

text.p: Iraq joined Iran and Saudi Arabia in the quarter-finals of the Asian Cup with a 4-1 (2-1 halftime) victory over Thailand in a group B match on Wednesday.
Strikers Hayder Majeed and Laith Shihaib scored two goals apiece in a match dominated by Iraq.

Majeed opened the scoring for Iraq in the 17th minute, tapping in a left flank cross. Six minutes later Shihaib made it two with a low 25-metre drive that beat goalkeeper Wacharapong Somcit on his right post.
Dusit Chalerman pulled one back for Thailand in the 26th minute when he trapped the ball unmarked in the Iraqi area and slotted it to the left of the 'keeper.
The Iraqis started the second half on the offensive, and in the 50th minute Majeed headed in a corner by Shihaib to restore Iraq's two goal advantage.

Shihaib grabbed his second and Iraq's fourth with the game's best goal in the 65th minute. He beat his marker before unleashing a right foot drive from 20-metres into the top corner of Wacharapong's goal.
The Iraqis had many other chances to increase their win but some slack finishing and fine goalkeeping denied them.
The result means the three Gulf sides ended their group B matches with six points each.

Iran topped the table by virtue of their 3-0 defeat of Saudi Arabia earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi's qualified in second place, and Iraq are guarenteed one of the quarter-final berths reserved for the two best third-placed teams in the three groups.
Thailand finished the 12-nation tournament without a point and are out.

Iraq - 1-Emad Hassan, 2-Samir Hassan, 3-Walid Afat (8-Mohamed Mahdi 80), 4-Abdul Jabar Hanoon, 5-Radhi Swadi, 6-Esam Salem, 7- Khalid Sabbar, 10-Qahtan Drain (11-Sahib Hassan 67), 12-Hayder Majeed, 15-Husam Naji (19-Ahmad Karin 53), 17-Laith Shihaib.

Thailand - 1-Wacharapong Somcit, 4-Phathanapang S, 5-Jakarat Tonhongsa, 6-Sanor Longsawang (20-Phithaya Santawong 82), 7- Natee Tongsukkao, 11-Yutthana Polsak, 14-Worrawooi Srimaka (15- Sunei Jaidee 73), 17-Dusit Chalermsan, 19-Surachai Jirasirichote, 22-Sing Totavee, 25-Sujja Sirikeat.
